title: Hazel and the Ghost
premise: Sable Kavanagh, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Office — an embassy that exists on no map — is repaid for a favor she has no memory of doing by a stranger named Hazel, who claims Sable once saved her life and now owes her seven days of help. Hazel's request drags Sable into a plot to stage a catastrophic 'accident' at a harbor summit, orchestrated from inside the very bureaucracy that employs her. As Sable discovers the attack is designed to erase evidence of the Office's crimes, she must choose between the rules that kept her alive and a justice no court will deliver. In the end, Sable exposes the conspirators at terrible personal cost, burns her old identity, and walks away with Hazel — belonging found not in an institution, but in loyalty freely given.
about_author: Yara Zhou is the pen name of a former policy analyst who spent years drafting documents she was never allowed to sign. She writes thrillers about people trapped between institutions and their consciences.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. A routine document burn in Vienna is interrupted when a woman named Hazel appears with proof of a rescue Sable never performed — dated, witnessed, and filed under Sable's real name. The emotional beat: unease; Sable's carefully compartmentalized world develops its first crack as debt becomes leverage.

chapters.title: Seven Days, Interest Owed
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Hazel invokes an old fixer's code: one favor returned with interest means seven days of unquestioned help. Her ask — access to Meridian shipping manifests — seems trivial until Sable cross-references them and finds a cargo vessel scheduled to dock during a closed-door harbor summit. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity hardening into dread.

chapters.title: Rules Rewritten
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Sable reports the anomaly through channels and watches her report vanish within hours; her security clearance is quietly downgraded. Her handler, Voss, warns her off with practiced warmth. Emotional beat: betrayal — the institution she served is not merely failing her but actively erasing her.

chapters.title: Hazel's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Sable/Hazel. Hazel reveals her own history: a whistleblower whose family died in a similar staged accident years ago, and who has spent a decade mapping the pattern. The emotional beat: two guarded women trading pieces of themselves over bad coffee; trust begins as transaction and edges toward something realer.

chapters.title: The Accident File
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Breaking into the Office's archive, Sable finds the operational file for the harbor event — complete with casualty projections and a scapegoat already chosen: herself. Emotional beat: cold terror sharpening into fury; survival now requires going outside every law she enforced.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: POV: Hazel. Hazel makes contact with a journalist while Sable runs counter-surveillance, but Voss's team is closer than either expected. A chase through the night market ends with Hazel wounded and the journalist's evidence half-destroyed. Emotional beat: desperation — the clock drops from days to hours, and the cost of the plan becomes blood.

chapters.title: What the Office Owes
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Confronting Voss privately, Sable learns the attack's true purpose: destroying the summit archives containing proof of decades of sanctioned atrocities. Voss offers her reinstatement if she lets it happen. Emotional beat: the book's moral crux — Sable stares at the price of survival and refuses to pay it.

chapters.title: Forty Minutes at Berth Nine
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. The climax: Sable and Hazel infiltrate the docks to stop the detonation and broadcast the archives simultaneously. Sable disables the charge while Hazel fights through Voss's team; the explosion fails, the files go public, and Voss dies by his own contingency protocol. Emotional beat: breathless, kinetic triumph shadowed by grief.

chapters.title: Aftermath Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. The fallout: headlines name a dead patsy, the Office disavows everything, and Sable is officially erased — her records purged, her pension voided. Justice arrived, but outside any courtroom, and it cost her the only identity she had. Emotional beat: hollow victory; freedom feels like falling until Hazel takes her hand.

chapters.title: A Door Left Open
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Weeks later, living under a new name in a coastal town, Sable receives a plain envelope: a ledger page showing one favor still owed — hers to Hazel, marked paid in full. For the first time, she belongs to no one's system but her own. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; the ghost was never Hazel, but the self Sable buried to survive.
